title: Market-intelligence lenses
tagline: Turning a graph of NYC AI rooms into four readable lenses (attended, research, market, job), fed by scheduled lanes and read every Monday.
why: Topic trends had quietly stopped absorbing new topics after 8 August. 102 of 272 topics had no theme, and 9 of the 25 events attended since 6 August added nothing to any trend. The health view's tripwire had been firing, but nothing alerted on it.
mission: A knowledge graph read through four lenses, sliceable by theme, segment, cohort and time. Each lens is fed by a lane, and every lane has a schedule, a run ledger, an alarm, a named consumer and a kill rule.
destination: Every lane writes on schedule and alarms when it goes quiet. A Monday Market Brief reads the lenses, so prep for any room starts from what moved that week, not from a blank page.
showcase: Diagnosing a silent data failure from the live database, and stating the do-nothing baseline before claiming a fix
Dimensional modelling for analytics: a slice contract with effective-dated theme membership, so a merge never breaks trend comparability
One guarded client for every pipeline write, with each schema change rehearsed on a twin database before it reaches production
Operating discipline for pipelines: each lane ships with a ledger, an alarm, a consumer and a kill rule, or it doesn't ship

metrics.note: The one left is unassigned on purpose until a theme fits it.

metrics.label: Research claims linked to a company or person
Recall vs akta (floor 0.60)
metrics.note: akta is the paid company-signals trial used as the reference. Recall is the share of akta's true signals that the candidate also found, matched on company, kind and date within 3 days. With dates shifted by 10 days, the null is 0.06–0.13 for the free stack and 0.07–0.18 for the free stack plus Clay. A blinded model labelled the signals. Alex's 20-label spot check agreed on 17 of 20, a first-party measurement from 2026-11-08.

decisions.decision: Replace the fixed 30-theme taxonomy with topics and subtopics that can group and evolve.
decisions.why: A fixed list kept dropping new subjects on the floor.

decisions.decision: Assign a topic to a theme at the moment it's created, in the session that has full context. The nightly job becomes a backstop.
decisions.why: The best embedding-only assigner reached 0.90 precision on just 5.9% of topics (PR #266).

decisions.decision: Build four lenses with sliceable cohorts instead of one trend view.
decisions.why: Thin data is a reason to ingest more, not to shrink the scope.

decisions.decision: Run the bake-off's paid leg on Clay credits already in hand instead of buying a news API first.
decisions.why: Measure before spending. The free stack's gap was deal and money news, which a third-party research agent could test on credits already in the workspace. The run used about 57.

decisions.decision: Lane 2 runs on the free stack plus Clay: free sources weekly, the Clay research agent every second week.
decisions.why: It was the only measured option that cleared the recall and coverage floors (0.69 and 0.88), and it costs credits rather than a new subscription.

open.question: Once the Clay credits already in hand run out (about two runs at the every-second-week cadence), buy credits or a Clay plan, or narrow the watchlist for the Clay leg?

risks.risk: The nightly health check is red while lane 1 stays in dry-run, and a red check can hide a real failure.
risks.mitigation: Take lane 1 writes live after its first Sunday run is checked.

risks.risk: Clay credits already in hand cover about two runs at the every-second-week cadence.
risks.mitigation: Decide on credits or a plan before they run out. The free stack keeps launch and incident news flowing either way.

log.text: Decision: lane 2 runs on the free stack plus Clay. The build has started.
Lane 2 bake-off: the free stack plus Clay reached 0.69 recall against akta (floor 0.60) and 0.88 coverage. The free stack alone reached 0.42 recall.
Lane 1's coverage alarm fired in the nightly check (issue #308). The structural checks passed.
Lane 2 bake-off run 1: the free stack is a launch and incident feed, not a deal feed.
Lanes 0 and 3 merged. Lane 4's table and fetcher passed review.
Backlog topics assigned to themes and three themes added.
Gap diagnosed on the live graph and the fix plan written.
